title: Left-cone restriction is cocartesian, with apex detection after base change
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], left join cones of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and cocartesian fibrations and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $K$ be any small simplicial set and $E$ a quasicategory in a fixed containing universe. Put $T=\Delta^0\star K$, with its cone vertex $v$, and let
$$r_E:\operatorname{Fun}(T,E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$$
be restriction. Then $r_E$ is a cocartesian fibration. An edge $\eta$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(T,E)$ is $r_E$-cocartesian if and only if its evaluation $\eta_v$ at the cone vertex is an equivalence edge of $E$.

For every quasicategory $B$ and simplicial functor $h:B\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$, form the degreewise pullback
$$P_h=B\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}\operatorname{Fun}(T,E).$$
It is a quasicategory and the projection $\pi:P_h\to B$ is a cocartesian fibration. An edge $(\alpha,\eta)$ of $P_h$ is $\pi$-cocartesian if and only if $\eta_v$ is an equivalence in $E$. The assertions allow empty $K$ and empty $B$; they assume no limits or colimits in $E$.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.7.5(1) (02VW), cone restriction and apex criterion; Remark 5.1.4.6 (01UF), cocartesian base change and detection of its cocartesian edges. Both read online 2026-10-17. These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion; shared archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$, $S=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0\star K,E)$, and let $p=(\operatorname{ev}_v,r_E):S\to E\times D$. Restriction along $K\subseteq\Delta^0\star K$ and along $\{v\}\amalg K\subseteq\Delta^0\star K$ is an isofibration by exponential restriction. Thus $S,D$ are quasicategories and $r_E,p$ are inner fibrations. Set $L=E\times_{\Delta_K,D,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)$. The joint projection $p_L:L\to E\times D$ is the pullback of the endpoint isofibration $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\to D\times D$, so $L$ is also a quasicategory. The join-cone comparison gives an equivalence $c:S\to L$ over $E\times D$, including an equivalence after fixing both the apex and the boundary. No fibration property of $\Delta_K:E\to D$ is asserted or required.

source.place: Agent expansion of the oriented-cone comparison in the proof of Corollary 5.3.7.4 (06MA); isofibration of restriction is Proposition 4.4.5.1 (01F1).

proof.text:
We first prove sufficiency of the apex test. Write a cone $X$ as $(a,F,\lambda)$ and a cone $Y$ as $(a',G,\mu)$. For $Z=(z,H,\nu)$, the join-cone mapping formula, transported along the mapping-space equivalences induced by the functor equivalence $c$ [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], identifies $\operatorname{Map}_S(X,Z)$ with
$$\operatorname{Map}_D(F,H)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}_D(\Delta_K a,H)}\operatorname{Map}_E(a,z).$$
An edge $u:X\to Y$ has boundary $b:F\to G$, apex $e:a\to a'$, and a coherent square $\mu\Delta_K(e)\simeq b\lambda$. Hence the pullback of $\operatorname{Map}_S(X,Z)$ along $b^*:\operatorname{Map}_D(G,H)\to\operatorname{Map}_D(F,H)$ is
$$\operatorname{Map}_D(G,H)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}_D(\Delta_K a,H)}\operatorname{Map}_E(a,z).$$
If $e$ is an equivalence, precomposition by $e$ and by $\Delta_K(e)$ is a weak equivalence on these mapping spaces: composing with their inverses gives homotopy inverses by associativity and the unit equations. Homotopy-pullback invariance, applied with the identity on $\operatorname{Map}_D(G,H)$ and these two equivalences, identifies the last display with $\operatorname{Map}_S(Y,Z)$. The comparison is the one induced by precomposition with $u$, because its path coordinate is the specified coherent square. Homotopy-pullback pasting justifies the displayed iterated pullback. Thus the mapping square for $u$ over $b$ is a homotopy pullback for every $Z$. The cocartesian mapping criterion implies that $u$ is $r_E$-cocartesian.

source.place: Agent-written mapping-space verification of the forward implication in Corollary 5.3.7.5(1).

proof.text: We construct a lift with identity apex. Given $X\in S$ with $cX=(a,F,\lambda)$ and an edge $b:F\to G$ of $D$, fill the inner $2$-horn $(\lambda,b)$ in $D$. Its composite $\lambda':\Delta_K a\to G$, together with the degenerate triangle on $1_{\Delta_K a}$, gives a square in $D$, hence an edge $cX\to t'=(a,G,\lambda')$ of $L$ with joint image $(1_a,b)$. The comparison on the fiber over $(a,G)$ is an equivalence. Choose $Y$ in that fiber and an equivalence $t'\to cY$ inside the same fiber. Composing gives an edge $\gamma:cX\to cY$ in $L$ whose joint image is homotopic, with endpoints fixed, to $(1_a,b)$. Since $c$ is a functor equivalence, it induces equivalences of mapping spaces [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. In particular choose an edge $u_0:X\to Y$ whose image has the component class of $\gamma$. Its joint image is therefore in the component of $(1_a,b)$ in $\operatorname{Map}_{E\times D}((a,F),(a,G))$. By the inner-mapping-fiber theorem, $p$ induces a Kan fibration on these mapping spaces. Lift a path from $p(u_0)$ to the vertex $(1_a,b)$, one edge at a time, to obtain an edge $u:X\to Y$ with $p(u)=(1_a,b)$ exactly. Vertices of the right-pinched mapping spaces are actual edges, so $u_v=1_a$ and $r_E(u)=b$. Step 2 makes $u$ cocartesian. Since $r_E$ is inner, these lifts prove that it is a cocartesian fibration.

source.place: Agent-written strict lifting argument; expands the existence of identity-apex lifts rather than applying the lax-comma theorem to a non-isofibration.

proof.text: For necessity, let $w:X\to Y$ be $r_E$-cocartesian over $b:F\to G$, and choose the identity-apex cocartesian lift $u:X\to Y'$ from Step 3. Both are initial in the quasicategory $L(X,b)$ of lifts. Their comparison gives an equivalence $s:Y'\to Y$ in the fiber over $G$ and a triangle $su\simeq w$. Evaluation at $v$ is a simplicial functor, so it carries the inverse and inverse triangles of $s$ to inverse data in $E$. Thus $s_v$ is an equivalence, and $w_v\simeq s_v1_a$ is an equivalence by the mapping-composition criterion for invertibility. Together with Step 2 this proves the asserted iff.

source.place: Agent expansion of the converse apex test of Corollary 5.3.7.5(1), using uniqueness of cocartesian lifts.

proof.text: Form $P_h=B\times_D S$. Inner lifting is preserved by this degreewise pullback: a prescribed simplex in $B$ gives its simplex in $D$, where the inner-fibration filler for $r_E$ supplies the $S$ coordinate. Since $B$ is a quasicategory, first fill its projected inner horn and then lift that simplex; this proves that $P_h$ is a quasicategory. If $u$ is $r_E$-cocartesian, its paired edge over an edge of $B$ is $\pi$-cocartesian: project each defining outer-horn problem to $S$, fill it using $u$, and pair the filler with the prescribed $B$ simplex. Step 3 therefore supplies cocartesian lifts for $\pi$. To check reflection, let $w=(\alpha,\eta)$ be $\pi$-cocartesian, and choose the lift $(\alpha,u)$ with identity apex. Initiality of these two lifts gives an equivalence between their targets in the fiber over the target of $\alpha$, with a comparison triangle. Projection to $S$ preserves that equivalence and triangle. Evaluating at the apex shows that $\eta_v$ is an equivalence, since $u_v$ is the identity. Conversely, if $\eta_v$ is an equivalence, Step 2 makes $\eta$ cocartesian and the outer-horn argument above makes $w$ cocartesian. For $K=\varnothing$, $S=E$, $D=\Delta^0$, and the statement is the equivalence-edge criterion for $E\to\Delta^0$; it is not an identity restriction. For empty $B$ the pullback is empty and all lifting conditions are vacuous. No step uses a limit or colimit in $E$.

source.place: Remark 5.1.4.6 (01UF), with preservation proved by horns and reflection by uniqueness of lifts.

proof_origin.place: Statement checked against Corollary 5.3.7.5(1) and Remark 5.1.4.6 (01UF). Independent mapping-space proof using the existing join-cone comparison, exponential restriction, and strict mapping-space path lifting; no hypothesis on the constant-diagram functor.
